name: Bianca Baker

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What fills a normal shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a contact centre team answering appliance warranty calls and chats. The hard ones are when a family has a broken refrigerator and three repair dates but no repairer; I can usually find who failed to book the visit. My two-year college diploma helped with the account rules, and I am one of the best on this floor. I earn the usual lead rate and have never used AI tools; I keep a written callback list.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What goes on at home after the shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband Ben lays flooring, and our children are nine and fourteen. We have a mortgage and about two months of expenses saved. A handful of other service centres are within a reasonable journey. Ben and I prefer steady paid work and keeping family commitments; neither of us wants to gamble the house on a fashionable idea.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that a shorter call note is fine if the repair appointment is real. A family with warm food in a broken refrigerator needs a named person to call back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my warranty team to keep working and the mortgage payments to stay regular. Two months saved is useful, but it would not last through a long gap in Ben’s flooring work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep my handwritten callback list and check each repair booking before I close a complaint. In the first year we will set aside part of Ben’s busy-month pay to bring our reserve closer to three months.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the job, though I always watch the next house bill. Little AI shortcuts do not change a broken refrigerator.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep the paper list?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The agent on the next shift can see who promised the callback. I have never used the AI note maker, and a missing name is too easy to miss.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which house bill worries you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The water heater is old. We can mend it when needed, but I would rather have the money ready than put the repair on credit.

I would keep a **named callback** for broken refrigerators.
think: I expect my **warranty team** to keep paid shifts.
I know **two months saved** cannot cover a long flooring-work gap.
do: Keep a **paper callback list** and check each repair booking.
Save from Ben’s **busy-month wages** toward three months of expenses.
feel: **Calm** about work, attentive to house bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor that a quick answer is no use if the repairer does not turn up. Management should show what happens to the paid shifts when booking moves to software.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect fewer ordinary calls and fewer agents, even if I keep the difficult warranty cases. My lead experience may protect my seat, but losing hours would press our mortgage budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask the manager for written shift plans and count missed repair visits for a month on my callback sheet. If the new answer system becomes compulsory, I will practise on closed warranty cases with a trainer during paid hours. If my rota falls in the first year, I will apply to posted paid warranty jobs nearby only where written wages and hours cover our mortgage and let us collect the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious about fewer paid hours. I do not like learning a new screen, but I will if the job requires it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you quit over the new system?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would keep the wage I have until a real written offer exists. I will not give notice because somebody says another centre is hiring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you check the new answer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare it with the repair booking and the callback date on ten closed cases. I would not start with a live family waiting on a fridge.

I would count **missed repair visits**, not only quick answers.
think: I expect **routine calls** and some seats to shrink.
I fear fewer **lead hours** would press the mortgage budget.
do: Keep my **callback sheet** and count missed visits.
Practise **required AI replies** on closed cases with a paid trainer.

fieldNote: She accepts **required AI practice** only with paid instruction.

steps.text: Keep logging missed warranty visits on written callback sheet

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that full thinking AI by 2028 could answer warranty calls and book visits. Hands-on robots around 2031 do not buy our headsets three years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the centre could close my shift. Two months saved and Ben’s flooring wage would not carry the mortgage and children for long if my pay stopped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask for written notice dates and put the planned patio purchase aside. If my role is threatened in the first year after 2028, I will look at posted paid building reception roles, but move only on a written offer with hours and wages covering the mortgage and school pickup. I will not resign early on a rumour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am alarmed. A good service record is thin shelter if nearly every customer question is answered elsewhere.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why building reception?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have greeted visitors when our centre desk was short, but that is not the same as running a building. I would ask to see a paid shift and its rota before calling it a plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for a course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a posted paid job requires it and pays the fee and time. I will not spend the mortgage reserve on a vague certificate.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** could answer warranty calls.
I would say **2031 robots** do not protect headset jobs.
think: I expect my **shift could close** despite strong service.
I know Ben’s **flooring wage** and two months saved cannot replace my income for long.
do: Request **written notice**, defer the patio and keep current paid shifts until a real written offer.
Complete a **required course** only for a posted paid vacancy funding fees and paid study time.
Move after threat only to **posted paid reception**, after checking paid shift/rota, with written mortgage-covering wages/hours and pickup.
feel: **Alarmed** by the fast threat to my wage.
S2.quote: A good service record is thin shelter if nearly every customer question is answered elsewhere.
fieldNote: Her visitor work is **limited experience**, not proof of a building job.
She rejects a **vague certificate** paid from the mortgage reserve.
A **written offer** must precede leaving her current pay.

steps.text: Delay the patio purchase while protecting the mortgage reserve

Move after threat only for posted paid reception with written mortgage-covering wages, hours and pickup
Complete required course only for posted paid job funding fees and paid study time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years is time to inspect a real workplace, not buy a course on a promise. General AI reaches our calls in 2031, with hands-on robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could stay on difficult warranty complaints for a while. I would rather see a real building shift before moving, since the reserve is for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep the warranty desk and ask a nearby building about a supervised paid reception day if it posts a place. If a paid vacancy has written wages and hours covering our mortgage and school pickup and funds its required safety course on paid time, I will complete it. In the first year after 2031 I will move only on a written offer meeting those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, though less rushed. Five years lets me check whether the early shift fits our home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you look for on the paid day?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would watch the first opening, visitor checks and who handles an injury. If the day is unpaid, it is not proof that I can earn there.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would Ben help decide?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My husband Ben and I would put his flooring calendar beside the new rota. One of us needs to be home for school pickup, and we cannot lose both wages at once.

I would distinguish **2031 calls** from later robots.

feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect a real shift.

fieldNote: A **paid trial** is needed to test income and opening duties.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a decade lets a family compare steady pay instead of chasing new job names. General AI reaches our desk in 2036 and hands-on robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I may still owe the mortgage, although the children could need us less after school. I would prefer to build six months of savings before making any risky change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep leading warranty calls and save some of each pay toward six months of expenses. Once a year I will look at posted reception work and ask what full paid hours it offers. If my call hours fall in the first year after 2036, I will move only for a written paid offer with wages and hours covering the mortgage, after Ben and I compare the family rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the long view, but steady enough now to save. I would rather keep paid work than look brave in a course photograph.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the savings target stalls?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If Ben’s flooring hours fall, the six-month target moves back. I will not borrow just to say we have saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell them that our home has to be paid for every month. An impressive title cannot make up for missing hours.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Two months saved will not cover a lost warranty wage for long. Written notice and a posted paid job with mortgage-covering hours would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who answers the family when a repairer never arrives, even if the booking screen says complete. Someone has to own that callback. A refrigerator does not start cooling because a case was closed.

headlineQuote: A refrigerator does not start cooling because a case was closed.
portrait: Bianca is a **43-year-old skilled lead** with a two-year college diploma and typical pay.
She has **never used AI** and relies on written callbacks for appliance warranty cases.
Her **two-month reserve**, mortgage, children and some nearby centres shape a cautious search.
She wants **posted paid work**, employer-funded required training and a written family-fitting wage before moving.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her warranty wage before a reliable new post appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice** and posted paid work with mortgage-covering hours would help.
